subject: Performance MAP: throughput & unit-economics — proposed test plan + checkpoints
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Kate Dawson <kate@catalyst-analytics.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@catalyst-analytics.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 5 Feb 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Performance MAP: throughput & unit-economics — proposed test plan + checkpoints

Kate / Samir —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Per our conversation I’m attaching a draft Mutual Action Plan (MAP) focused on the performance evaluation you requested. High-level goals: validate latency / TTFT & sustained throughput targets at 95th percentile, measure tokens/sec and sustained QPS under your expected concurrency profile, and produce a concise unit-economics summary (cost per 1M tokens + projected monthly costs).

Proposed milestones (see attached XLSX for details):
- Week 0 (Feb 8): confirm canonical prompt set and target scenarios (streaming chat, batch generation).
- Week 1 (Feb 9–13): run baseline single-instance benchmarks (p50/p95 TTFT, tokens/sec at concurrency 1).
- Week 2 (Feb 14–16): stress tests across concurrency vector [1,4,8,16], sustained 30-min windows for each step to capture thermal behavior.
- Week 3 (Feb 17–20): run cost modeling + produce MAP results deck.

Key acceptance criteria we recommend including in MAP:
- p95 TTFT (time-to-first-token) <= 300ms for streaming chat workload (avg response length 120 tokens)
- sustained tokens/sec >= 3,000 for your high-throughput batch generator at concurrency 8
- steady-state QPS >= 20 for 128-token payloads under 8 concurrent clients
- Unit economics: full-coverage cost-per-1M-tokens modeling with sensitivity to batching and quantization (we’ll supply two model variants).

I’ve attached the draft MAP + a blank prompt set template. Please confirm that the sample prompts are representative and tell us whether you want us to run tests in your VPC or on Redwood hosted infra.

Next step: quick sync (15m) to lock prompts and environment. Are you available Feb 8 at 10:00am PT?

Best,
Rishi
Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Kate — great, thanks for the notes. I updated the attached XLSX and bumped the target response length to 160 tokens across the batch scenarios. Confirming Redwood-hosted for the initial runs; we’ll schedule a VPC validation once the baseline passes.

Quick outline of what we’ll measure during the stress window (Feb 14–16):
- Metrics: p50/p90/p95 TTFT, tokens/sec (aggregate across workers), sustained QPS (requests/sec), GPU utilization, and per-request token cost (raw and amortized with batching).
- Test cadence: 30-minute sustained window per concurrency point with warmup of 10 minutes, sample at 1-second resolution.
- Variants: Model A (unquantized; higher perf/quality) and Model B (int8 quantized; cost-optimized) — we’ll supply both results.

Attaching the revised MAP and a CSV template we’ll populate during runs. I’ll run the first baseline on Feb 11 and send a raw results dump after the run.

Rishi

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Kate Dawson <kate@catalyst-analytics.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@catalyst-analytics.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 16:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Final MAP deliverable: benchmark results + unit-economics summary (attached)

Kate / Samir —

Please find the completed MAP deliverable attached. Below is an executive summary of the key metrics from the Feb 14–15 runs (Redwood-hosted environment, Model A = baseline FP16, Model B = int8 quantized). Full CSV attached (benchmark-results-20260215.csv) and a concise cost model PDF.

Executive summary:
- Environment: 4x A100 (80GB) worker cluster; autoscaling disabled for test windows; 10-minute warmup excluded from steady-state windows.
- Workload: batch generator (160-token target), streaming chat (avg 48 tokens).

Model A (FP16):
- p50 TTFT (streaming chat): 95 ms
- p95 TTFT (streaming chat): 230 ms
- Tokens/sec (sustained, concurrency 8): 3,420 tokens/sec (aggregate across 4 GPUs)
- Normalized tokens/sec per GPU: 855 tokens/sec/GPU
- Sustained QPS (128-token payload, concurrency 8): 26.7 QPS
- Observations: minimal drift during 30-min windows; avg GPU util 72%.

Model B (int8 quantized):
- p50 TTFT: 110 ms
- p95 TTFT: 270 ms
- Tokens/sec (sustained, concurrency 8): 4,180 tokens/sec (aggregate)
- Normalized tokens/sec per GPU: 1,045 tokens/sec/GPU
- Sustained QPS (128-token payload): 32.6 QPS
- Observations: quantized path improved throughput ~22% vs FP16 with a small p95 TTFT regression (~40ms).

Concurrency sweep (160-token batch) — steady-state tokens/sec aggregate:
- concurrency 1: 520 tokens/sec
- concurrency 4: 1,860 tokens/sec
- concurrency 8: 4,180 tokens/sec
- concurrency 16: 6,200 tokens/sec (note: latency p95 increases ~15% due to queuing at 16)

Unit economics (cost-per-1M-tokens):
- Model A (FP16, no batching optimizations): $3.20 / 1M tokens
- Model B (int8, standard batching): $1.95 / 1M tokens
- Aggressive batching + KV cache assumptions (best-case): $1.20 / 1M tokens

Projected monthly cost for Catalyst baseline (estimated 500M tokens / month):
- Model A: $1,600 / month
- Model B: $975 / month
- Best-case (aggressive batching): $600 / month

Files attached: benchmark-results-20260215.csv (raw samples at 1s resolution), cost-model-catalyst-20260216.pdf (concise cost sensitivity tables).

Next steps we propose:
- VPC validation window (Feb 22–24) to confirm parity in your network.
- Final MAP sign-off (we’ll add the sensitivity table Jonas requested to the PDF).

If these numbers look good to you I’ll prepare a short one-page SLA note and a recommended Dedicated capacity configuration for your expected peak.

Best,
Rishi
Account Executive
Redwood Inference
